name: InitCore Commerce
headline: Sell online and run every order from one back office.
summary: An online store and its back office built as one system — products, stock, checkout, shipping, offers and reports — for Indian retailers who sell from shops and online.
description: InitCore Commerce is a complete online store with the back office to run it. Shoppers search with suggestions that forgive typos, see live stock and a dated delivery window, and check out on one page with express delivery, store pickup, cash on delivery or online payment.

The owner sees what needs attention on one dashboard, moves orders through clear steps, ships them in one or more parcels with carrier and tracking, handles returns and refunds, keeps stock per warehouse and store, reorders by supplier, runs offers and email campaigns, and reads sales reports and a visit-to-order funnel.

It is InitCore's own build in Angular, .NET and PostgreSQL, made for India from the first line — rupees, GST-inclusive prices, PIN codes, COD, Razorpay and store pickup — and tested from unit to browser level.
challenge: Retailers who sell from shops and online usually juggle a website plugin, payment links, a stock spreadsheet and phone calls about deliveries. The website doesn't know what's on the shelf, offers are applied by hand, and no one can see sales and reorders in one place.
solution: One system with two halves: a storefront with typo-tolerant search, dated delivery, a one-page checkout and order tracking; and a back office for orders, parcels, returns, stock per location, reorders, promotions, campaigns, staff permissions and reports.
highlights: Storefront and back office share one database
One-page checkout with COD, Razorpay, express delivery and store pickup
Ship in parcels; customers see every carrier update
Dashboard of what needs attention, reorder list by supplier
Promotions, campaigns, reports and a shopping funnel
7 staff permission areas and an audit log

name: InitCore CRM
headline: Every lead, call, sale and shift on one screen.
summary: A CRM for outbound call centres. Leads are shared out, every call gets an outcome, verified payments become invoice PDFs, and owners see sales and attendance live.
description: InitCore CRM runs the day of an outbound call centre. Lead sheets are imported from CSV or Excel, matched to the right fields once, and shared out to teams and agents in bulk. Importing the same list again updates leads instead of duplicating them.

Agents record how each call ended, add a remark and set call-back reminders that count down on the lead. When a customer pays, the payment is recorded against the lead; when the owner verifies it, the invoice PDF is created on the spot with GSTIN, tax and the amount in words.
Owners and team leaders see sales against target, attendance worked out from login and logout, breaks as they happen and every agent's call outcomes. Each role sees only its own slice of the data.
challenge: An outbound call centre works from lists. Once a list is shared, answers scatter across Excel, WhatsApp groups and a register: who called this number last, which call-backs are due, which payments came in and whether the invoice went out, who is on break, and who is close to target. Two agents call the same customer, call-backs are forgotten and invoices are typed by hand.
solution: One web app that follows a lead from the sheet it arrived in to the invoice it ended with: lead import with column mapping, bulk assignment with a full history, call outcomes with reminders, payments matched to leads, invoice PDFs on verification, a live break monitor, automatic attendance, a target leaderboard and reports — scoped to owner, team leader and agent.
highlights: Payment verified → invoice PDF ready, with GSTIN, tax and amount in words
Every call ends with an outcome, a remark and an optional call-back reminder
Live break monitor that updates without a refresh
Attendance from login and logout, with break time subtracted
Agents ranked against their monthly target
Lead import from CSV or Excel with column mapping and no duplicate numbers
Three roles — owner, team leader, agent — on the same pages

name: InitCore Real Estate
headline: Every bed, tenant and rupee of rent in one place
summary: Property management software for a co-living operator. Every bed is tracked with its own rent and status, new tenants are invited to a specific bed by email, rent is recorded against the bed, and tenants and landlords get their own portals.
description: A co-living business rents beds, not flats. This web app tracks every property down to the individual bed, with its own rent, deposit and status: occupied, free, reserved or under repair. Room occupancy is worked out from the beds, so it is always up to date.

When a bed frees up, staff email a prospect an invitation for that exact bed, and the bed is held as reserved. The prospect registers from the link without an account and sees the bed, rent and deposit. The owner reviews the application next to the bed and approves it, which creates the tenant's account and sends a welcome email.

Rent and other payments are recorded against the tenant, room and bed, and late payments are flagged. Contracts show the days remaining, and agreements ending soon are flagged. Tenants and landlords each have their own portal, staff roles control access module by module, and support tickets and new enquiries are tracked alongside.
challenge: The operator rents beds, not flats. One room can have several tenants, a free bed and a different rent for each, and every bed has its own move-in date, deposit and agreement end date. Spreadsheets and WhatsApp could not show which beds were free, who had paid, or which agreements were about to end.
solution: One web app built around beds: properties, rooms and beds with their own rent and status; email invitations tied to a specific bed with self-registration and approval; rent and payments recorded against the bed; contracts with expiry warnings; support tickets with deadlines; a leads pipeline; role-based staff access; and portals for tenants and landlords.
highlights: Every property tracked down to the individual bed, with its own rent, deposit and status.
Invite a prospect to a specific bed by email; the bed is held as reserved until they apply.
Applications reviewed next to the bed and approved in two clicks.
Rent recorded against tenant, room and bed, with upcoming, pending and overdue amounts on one screen.
Agreements ending within 30 days flagged to staff and to the tenant.
Separate portals for tenants and landlords, and role-based access for staff.

headline: A property website the team updates from one Google Sheet.
summary: A fast real estate website for a MahaRERA-registered channel partner. The team edits listings in a Google Sheet, and every floor plan is one tap from WhatsApp.
description: Key2YourHome is a MahaRERA-registered real estate channel partner covering Thane, Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Pune. Its prices and stock change every week, and its sales happen on WhatsApp.
I built a static website that takes every listing from one Google Sheet. When the team edits a row, the site rebuilds and publishes itself, with no server, database or admin panel to maintain.

Buyers filter by city, BHK and budget, open full-screen floor plans, and tap "Get price" to start a WhatsApp chat with the unit and project already typed. Callback requests land in the Sheet and the sales inbox.
challenge: Listings, prices and stock change every week, and every website update used to need a developer. Buyers want floor plans, prices and proof of MahaRERA registration before they talk to anyone, and the sales team needs to know which project and unit each enquiry is about.
solution: A static Astro website that reads every listing from one Google Sheet at build time and rebuilds automatically when the Sheet changes. Each project gets a full page with gallery, facts, unit plans and its MahaRERA number; every unit has a pre-filled WhatsApp enquiry; callback requests are written to the Sheet by a Google Apps Script and emailed to sales.

name: NOVEM
headline: Know what sells, who is leaving, and what to do next.
summary: A desktop app for online store owners. Drop in your sales exports and it shows what is working, which customers are slipping away, and what to do next — all on your own computer.
description: Most online stores run on exports and spreadsheets. The built-in reports say revenue went down, but not why, or what to do about it — and proper analytics tools are priced for companies that already employ an analyst.

NOVEM reads the exports a store already has (CSV, Excel, Google Sheets, Shopify or PostgreSQL), checks every row, and turns them into a dashboard, customer segments, ad-spend checks, 30-day forecasts and a ranked list of next steps with an estimated value against each.
It runs entirely on the owner's laptop. Customer names and emails are scrambled on import, there is no account to create, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
challenge: Small online stores have plenty of data in exports but no analyst. Built-in reports stop at 'revenue went down', enterprise BI is too expensive, and most analytics services want the customer list on their servers.
solution: A local-first desktop app with a full import pipeline (detect, map, clean, hash personal data, score quality, merge) and an analytics engine that segments customers, predicts who will stop buying, checks ad spend against stock, forecasts the next 30 days and turns the findings into recommended actions — explained in plain language.
highlights: Imports a Shopify export with columns matched automatically and every row validated
Scores each customer's chance of buying again
Flags ad campaigns still spending on out-of-stock products
Recommended actions ranked by estimated rupee value
What-if simulator for price and acquisition changes
Runs offline on your own computer — no account, nothing uploaded

name: S.K Trading — Billing App
headline: Quotation to GST invoice in one click, with the printed page live
summary: A Windows billing app for an industrial valve trader. Quotations, proformas, GST invoices and delivery challans come from one screen, with the printed page building as you type.
description: S.K Trading & Co. supplies valves, pipes and fittings to industry from Navi Mumbai. Every order needs a quotation, a proforma invoice, a GST tax invoice and a delivery challan, each repeating the same customer, items and rates.

I built a Windows desktop app that makes all four from one screen, offline on the office PC. The printed A4 page sits beside the form and updates as you type. 'Create as…' turns a quotation into a proforma, invoice or challan in one click, and GST splits into CGST + SGST or IGST from the state.

Customers and products build themselves from past documents, so details and HSN codes fill in and the last rate for each customer is shown. One tick marks an invoice paid, reports are ready for the CA, and documents go out by email or WhatsApp with the PDF ready.
challenge: A valve and pipe stockist was producing four documents per order (quotation, proforma, tax invoice and delivery challan), retyping the same customer, items and rates each time, with GSTINs, HSN codes and the CGST/SGST-vs-IGST split easy to get wrong and no quick view of who still owed money.
solution: An offline Windows billing app with one editor for all four documents, a live A4 preview on the company letterhead, one-click conversion between documents, automatic GST, self-building customer and product lists, paid/unpaid tracking, reports for the CA, email and WhatsApp sending, and Google Drive backup.
highlights: Quotation, proforma, tax invoice and delivery challan from one screen.
A live A4 print preview: what you see is what prints.
'Create as…' turns a quotation into an invoice or challan in one click.
CGST/SGST or IGST, rounding and amount in words worked out automatically.
Customer and product details fill in, with each customer's last rate.
Paid/unpaid in one tick, with outstanding per customer.
Works offline, with backup to Google Drive and automatic updates.

name: S.K Trading & Co.
headline: A website that turns product searches into quote requests, and an admin that follows every one up
summary: A fast product catalogue website for an industrial valves and pipes supplier, built around the quote request, with a private admin for enquiries, follow-ups, WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, email, contacts and stock.
description: S.K Trading & Co. is an independent supplier and stockist of industrial valves, MS pipes and pipe fittings in Navi Mumbai, supplying contractors, resellers and industry since 2019.
I built its new website: 34 products in three categories, 20 detailed product pages, a product finder on the first screen, and a quote form that opens with the product already filled in.

Behind it, a private admin works as the owner's command centre: quote requests with status, notes and follow-up reminders; WhatsApp chats and catalogue campaigns; Facebook and Instagram posts made from any product; email campaigns; one contact book; stock status that shows on the website within a minute; and alerts on the phone and desktop.
challenge: Industrial buyers don't shop; they ask whether a product is supplied, in which size and standard, and for a quote. The supplier needed a website that answers those questions and makes the quote request the easiest step, strictly honest (a supplier, not a manufacturer or authorised dealer). Then the owner needed to act on every enquiry and reach buyers on WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram and email without juggling five apps.
solution: A prerendered Next.js website on Cloudflare with a product finder, live search, detailed product pages and a quote form that carries the product. Behind it, a private admin on Cloudflare D1 and R2: a dashboard of what needs attention, enquiries and follow-ups, a contact book, WhatsApp Business chats and template campaigns, Facebook and Instagram posting with scheduling, email campaigns through Hostinger Reach, one-click stock status, a product editor with a reviewed publish step, Web Push alerts and a connection map checked every 30 minutes.
highlights: 34 products in 3 categories, 20 detailed product pages
Quote form pre-filled with the product
Enquiries with status, notes and follow-up reminders
WhatsApp chats and catalogue campaigns in the admin
Facebook and Instagram posts from any product, scheduled
Phone and desktop alerts, with quiet hours and a 9 am summary
43 automated tests at 3 screen sizes

name: Taj Metals
headline: Every product one tap from a WhatsApp quote.
summary: A website for a Mumbai tube and pipe supplier, built around WhatsApp: full specifications on every product and a quote message that already names the product.
description: Taj Metals supplies ready-to-hone tubes, hydraulic, seamless, rectangular and ERW pipes and boiler tubes from Mumbai. Its buyers enquire on WhatsApp, usually without naming a product.
I built the website around WhatsApp: one file holds the number and five message templates, so every button writes the right request, and each product page opens a chat that names the product.
Product pages carry full specifications; visitors filter by material and standard; FAQs, three buyer guides and structured data help the right buyers find the right pipe.
challenge: Buyers enquire on WhatsApp with messages like "price?", so the team spends the first reply asking which product, grade and size. There was no catalogue online for Google to show.
solution: A Next.js product website with WhatsApp as the only contact channel. Five message templates in one file power every button; product pages show full specifications and open a chat naming the product. Filters, FAQs, buyer guides, structured data and a sitemap complete it.
highlights: WhatsApp quote that names the product, from every product page
